_readme: FIRST-DRAFT config for TaS2005's new corner marker (a larger, tick-flanked
winged-cross, visually distinct from this dataset's own plain grid crosshairs --
see markers.py/config.py for the marker_template_path /
non_substrate_mask_open_px fields added specifically to support this).
TaS2005_marker_template.png was REGENERATED once already: the first version
was missing the marker's own upper arm (cropped away by mistake, mistaking a
short region for stray text) -- looked visibly asymmetric/truncated on
inspection. Corrected by connected-component-selecting the true marker parts
(upper arm, core, left/right tick, lower tail -- 5 separate components,
confirmed disjoint from the adjacent "K" letter text) directly from the same
source image, rather than a blunt rectangular crop. The real marker is fully
symmetric: upper arm and lower tail both measure exactly 94px. Re-verified
end-to-end after the fix (both raw-image and real reconstructed-pipeline
paths) -- positions now match the core's own true measured center (587,158)
even more precisely than the first version did.
Verified end-to-end against a real image
(\\132.68.73.70\Data\Ilay\TaS2005\Post Exfo\QK.png, which shows both the
top-left and top-right corner markers) run through the ACTUAL pipeline flow --
channel_selection.select_and_reconstruct (reusing
channels_model/outputs/channels_model.onnx, the same model Ta2009/TS34001/
TaS2011/example_config already share -- NOT yet verified for TaS2005's own
substrate color specifically, only visually spot-checked as looking clean/
correctly posterized) followed by find_top_markers on ITS reconstructed
output, exactly matching run.py's own real call sequence (NOT just the raw
photo, which was this file's own earlier, weaker claim). Both real markers
correctly located. With the regenerated (symmetric) template: substrate-mask-
alone only clears crosshair_whole_match_threshold (0.5) for the right marker
(0.54); otsu-mask-alone clears BOTH cleanly (0.72 right, 0.62 left) with a
comfortable gap (0.10+) over the next-best plain-grid-cross false-candidate
(0.53) -- find_top_markers' own designed substrate-then-otsu-then-pooled
fallback cascade (see its docstring) is what makes this work in practice, not
a single mask being independently sufficient. Not a bug, but means don't
assume substrate-mask-alone success on future TaS2005 images either.
marker_refine_half_px is 55, not this codebase's usual 90: found and fixed a
REAL bug via this same real-image test -- at half=90, _refine_marker_center
silently latched onto a fragment of the adjacent "K"/"!" text label (which
sits only ~5-30px from this marker's own core, much closer than other
datasets' markers sit to their own nearest text) instead of the real core,
moving a correct position 65px off with NO error/warning -- the same class of
bug config.py's marker_refine_max_aspect docstring already documents for
Ta2009, just triggered here by TaS2005's own tighter marker-to-text spacing.
Swept half_px 48-90 directly against the real reconstructed image: behavior
is genuinely non-monotonic/chaotic in 62-90 (sometimes the tail, sometimes
text, sometimes correct by luck) -- no reliable window in that range found
real refinement without risking contamination. 48-60 reliably falls back to
the already-accurate coarse (whole-template) position instead (documented,
intended behavior of _refine_marker_center when no qualifying blob is found --
never guesses) -- chosen over chasing genuine sub-pixel refinement given how
unpredictable the contamination boundary was on real data.
crosshair_use_arm_triangulation is deliberately FALSE here (every other
dataset has it True): that strategy triangulates a center from 2-3
surviving radiating arms, which doesn't semantically apply to this
marker's disconnected tick-mark topology -- left disabled rather than
risk a nonsense candidate on some future image, since (unlike the two
masks below) it's not something this one test image could validate
either way (it produced zero candidates here, on either mask -- see
next paragraph -- so this image never actually exercised it).
core+arm-evidence (crosshair_core_*/crosshair_arm_*, no off-switch
exists in markers.py -- it runs unconditionally, unlike arm
triangulation) is carried over UNCHANGED from TaS2011.json. Directly
tested on this real image (markers._find_candidates with both masks):
it produced ZERO candidates here, same as arm-triangulation -- so this
one test didn't corrupt the result, but that means UNEXERCISED, not
validated; it may behave differently (including produce a wrong
candidate that competes with the real one, since all strategies pool
into one ranked list -- see _find_candidates's own docstring) on a
future image where a core-shaped blob happens to appear. Watch for
this specifically on early real runs.
Also NOT yet verified: the shared channels_model's reconstruction quality
on TaS2005's own substrate specifically (spot-checked visually only, on
one image); the bottom-left/bottom-right corner markers (cut off in the
one sample image available so far); marker_refine_half_px=55 on a second
real letter (only "K"/"!" tested -- "L" at the other corners has a
different shape/width, so its own safe-window boundary could differ).
Re-verify all of the above against more real TaS2005 images, ideally
covering all 4 corners and any low-contrast/partial cases, before
trusting this in production.
detection_config_path below points to flake_detection/config/TaS2005.json,
itself only substrate_hsv_range-verified (see that file's own readme) --
not a validated flake-detection config.
_comment_detection_config_path: DetectionConfig JSON reused for flake color range and marker pink/bright ranges — keep this in sync with whatever flake_detection used to find these images.
_comment_flake_detection_output_dir: A flake_detection run's own --output folder (contains contours/). If set, each image's flakes/<stem>.json in THIS run's output gets flake_detection's real per-flake contour+score, transformed through this image's own calibration -- what contact_placement consumes. Leave null to skip (flakes/<stem>.json will just be empty).
_comment_channel_selection: No TaS2005-specific trained channels_model exists -- reusing channels_model/outputs/channels_model.onnx, the same one Ta2009/TS34001/TaS2011/example_config already share (real precedent for cross-dataset reuse in this codebase). NOT yet verified for TaS2005's own substrate color (notably different/more saturated purple-violet than TS34001's, per flake_detection/config/TaS2005.json's measured substrate_hsv_range) -- reconstruction quality needs checking directly, not assumed, before trusting downstream steps (marker detection now runs against THIS reconstructed image in the real run() pipeline, not the raw photo -- see run.py line ~152).
_comment_markers: See this file's own _readme above for what's verified vs. carried over untested. marker_template_path points at the new TaS2005-specific template (larger, tick-flanked marker) instead of the shared crosshair_template.png every other dataset uses. non_substrate_mask_open_px=3 cleans up real background speckle noise confirmed on this dataset's own substrate (see markers._non_substrate_mask's own docstring) -- 0 (off) on every other dataset, deliberately not a shared default.
_comment_interactive_alignment: If true, grid_preperation.run pops an interactive window between marker detection and everything else: drag the red (left/filename) and green (right) crosshair crosses to correct their position on any image, including placing both from scratch where automatic detection failed. Save writes a permanent per-image override (marker_overrides/<stem>.json) that skips automatic detection on every future run. Through all_code.py this is also gated by PipelineConfig.interactive (config/pipeline_config.json) -- both must be true to actually see it.
_comment_placement: PLACEHOLDER values copied from TaS2011.json -- grid_pitch_um/placement offsets must be confirmed against TaS2005's own real chip/grid geometry before trusting placement in production.
_comment_polygon_export: PLACEHOLDER values copied from TaS2011.json -- not re-verified for TaS2005.
_comment_color_palette: Each exported polygon is colored to match its own real channels_model cluster color -- but no trained model exists for TaS2005 yet (see channels_model_onnx_path above), so this only matters once one is trained.
_comment_output: template_cif_path is only ever read, never modified in place -- it's copied once into --output and every placement is spliced into that working copy. Set to null to skip placement entirely (same effect as --no-placement).
